rendered: After cycling at higher rates, the cathode delivers 306 mAh[1] per gram of sulfur at the long-cycle point (the paper's own sulfur-based figure). With respect to the entire electrode mass, it delivers 87 mAh/g[2] after the same cycling. The ratio of these values implies a sulfur share of the electrode of 28.4%[3], against the moderate sulfur loading the paper states: 35 wt % active sulfur[4]. The implied share is therefore lower than the stated sulfur content.
